# Links

**Foundation group:** typography  
**Reviewed against:** GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 on 2026-09-09

Use descriptive, underlined GOV.UK links for navigation and preserve their visited, hover, active and focus states.

## Rules

- Links are blue and underlined by default; linked text at the end of a sentence must not include the full stop.
- Write link text that describes the destination or result when read out of context.
- Use govuk-link--no-visited-state only where visited history is not useful, such as frequently changing application navigation.
- Use the official inverse or no-underline variants only in their documented contexts.
- If a link opens a new tab, warn users in the link text and avoid doing so unless necessary.

## Accessibility contract

- Retain the visible underline and GOV.UK focus treatment; colour alone must not identify a link.
- Avoid repeated vague labels such as click here or read more.
- Keep the anchor href so links work with keyboards, assistive technology and without JavaScript.

## Restrictions and caveats

- Do not style ordinary navigation links as buttons.
- Do not remove visited styling globally merely for visual uniformity.

## Token references

- `govuk.color.link`
- `govuk.color.link-visited`
- `govuk.color.link-hover`
- `govuk.color.link-active`
- `govuk.color.focus`
- `govuk.color.focus-text`

## Examples

### Link in body content

```html
<p class="govuk-body">Read the <a class="govuk-link" href="/eligibility">eligibility guidance</a>.</p>
```
